Article Title: 'Gang of dacoits': Yogi Adityanath says Akhilesh must apologise for UP 'loot and extortion'
Article Text:
Adityanath also revisited the issue of encephalitis, which he said had caused widespread fear in eastern Uttar Pradesh for decades.

Adityanath says UP has left 'BIMARU' image behind

CM attacks SP-Congress over encephalitis deaths

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday attacked the Samajwadi Party , calling it a "gang of dacoits" and accusing its leadership of looting the state exchequer during its tenure.Speaking in Deoria, he said SP president Akhilesh Yadav should apologise to the people of Uttar Pradesh over the alleged financial irregularities linked to the construction of the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow.Adityanath made the remarks while laying the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth more than Rs 305 crore in Deoria. He also contrasted the current state government with previous administrations, claiming that Uttar Pradesh had moved away from an image associated with poor governance, insecurity and the influence of criminal networks."SP means loot and extortion, SP means a gang of dacoits," Adityanath said.He directly targeted Akhilesh Yadav over the alleged misuse of public funds, saying, "For the loot of the state exchequer that the SP chief committed for his indulgence, he should apologise to the people," he said, referring to alleged corruption in the construction of the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow.The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh had previously been dominated by what he described as a "parallel government of mafias".He claimed the situation had changed under his administration, with criminal networks being dismantled and the state's image improving."Now UP has a good image. Mafias have been reduced to dust. Those who breach the security of daughters and traders have only two places to go -- they are either in jail or in hell," Adityanath said.He also linked development and governance to the election of "good public representatives", saying that the state's progress was a result of the choices made by voters."When good public representatives are elected, good governments come and the results are also good. This development, prosperity and employment are the result of the hard work of the public representatives whom you elected," he said.The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh had faced a severe deficit in development and public services before 2017."Before 2017, there was neither development nor security nor respect in Uttar Pradesh. There was no employment, nor houses, toilets, LPG connections, electricity and roads for the poor. Schools had become centres of cheating," he said.Adityanath also revisited the issue of encephalitis, which he said had caused widespread fear in eastern Uttar Pradesh for decades. He identified Deoria, Maharajganj, Gorakhpur, Siddharthnagar, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Basti among the districts that were particularly affected between July 15 and November 15 each year."This was not a disease; it was the sick mentality of the SP-Congress governments. In 40 years, 50,000 innocent children died, but no chief minister or prime minister from the SP or the Congress came to take stock of the situation," Adityanath said.The chief minister also invoked the term 'BIMARU', which was coined by demographer Ashish Bose in the mid-1980s to describe Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, then among India's poorest states.Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had now moved beyond that description, pointing to improvements in development, security and infrastructure as evidence of the state's transformation.Agriculture minister Surya Pratap Shahi, minister of state for rural development Vijay Lakshmi Gautam, and MLAs Shalabh Mani Tripathi and Sabha Kunwar Kushwaha were among those present at the Deoria programme.
Article Summary: Adityanath says up has left 'bimaru' image behind. Cm attacks sp-congress over encephalitis deaths in eastern uttar pradesh. He says sp means loot and extortion, sp means a gang of dacoits. "those who breach the security of daughters and traders have only two places to go," he says.

Article Title: 'Will you suspend them for backstabbing Sikhs?' AAP asks BJP over MPs' visit to Sajjan Kumar's home
Article Text:
AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj questions BJP over BJP MPs visit to Sajjan Kumar's residence (File photo/PTI)

NEW DELHI: The AAP on Saturday challenged the BJP to take action against three of the party’s Lok Sabha MPs from Delhi for attending the condolence meeting of former Congress leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.Kumar, 80, died in Delhi on August 20 while serving life imprisonment in a case related to the anti-Sikh riots.According to BJP leader HS Phoolka, an advocate who represented victims of the 1984 violence and their families, party MPs Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri, and Yogender Chandolia visited Kumar's residence to offer condolences following his death.AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj claimed that the BJP was “sympathetic” towards Kumar, alleging that the saffron party had “helped” the Congress in targeting Sikh families during the 1984 riots."Some people do say that during the anti-Sikh riots in Delhi, local BJP/RSS leaders helped congress in targeting innocent Sikh families on the streets of Delhi. Is this the reason why top BJP leaders of Delhi are so sympathetic to Sajjan Kumar?" Bharadwaj posted on X."Will @NitinNabin suspend these MPs of BJP who have backstabbed Sikhs?" he added, tagging the BJP national president.Bhardwaj also questioned the “silence” of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leaders on the issue.SAD leaders have repeatedly indicated that the party may join hands with its former ally, the BJP, for the upcoming assembly elections in Punjab, where the AAP is currently in power.His post came after BJP leader HS Phoolka, an advocate who represented victims of the 1984 violence and their families, strongly criticised the BJP leaders for visiting Kumar’s residence.“Strongly condemn the visit of 3 MPs Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri and Yogender Chandolia to mass murderer Sajjan Kumar's residence to offer condolences on his death. This is when the BJP has always supported our quest for justice against these culprits and supported us in ensuring that he stays in jail. Sympathy should be reserved for victims and their families—many of whom live the horror of those days even till now,” Phoolka wrote.Phoolka also called for a “boycott” of the three MPs.The anti-Sikh riots broke out following the October 31, 1984, assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards. The assassination came months after the Army’s Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab, in June 1984.
Article Summary: Aap delhi chief saurabh bharadwaj questions bjp over bjp mps visit to sajjan kumar's residence. Kumar, 80, died in delhi on august 20 while serving life imprisonment in a case related to the 1984 anti-sikh riots.

Article Title: ‘Do you feel you are a lord?’ Bombay HC slams FDA, clears reopening of 5 eateries
Article Text:
The bench also questioned why the FDA acted with “undue haste” without fully analysing the legal position.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on slammed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), warning of contempt action against officials after the department refused to lift the suspension of food licences of five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises despite a fresh inspection finding them 88% compliant with food safety rules.“Tired of scolding the department and officers,” the division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said the FDA had taken a “pedantic instead of pragmatic view” despite the court’s earlier direction to reconsider the matter. The court ultimately vacated the suspension orders, allowing the five eateries at the MCA premises in Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) to reopen.The MCA had challenged the FDA’s decision to suspend the restaurants’ licences over alleged hygiene violations and issues relating to third-party operations. A fresh inspection conducted on Thursday found the eateries to be 88% compliant with food safety requirements.However, the FDA had initially continued with the suspension, citing the fact that the restaurants were being operated by M/s Shirke Infrastructure, while the licences were registered in the MCA’s name.On Saturday, the FDA told the court that it would issue a fresh notice to the MCA, give it an opportunity to be heard on its contractual arrangement with Shirke Infrastructure and then pass a reasoned order.Accepting the undertaking, the court said the restaurants could reopen since the latest inspection had found them compliant. “There is no provision in the law that prohibits the same,” the bench observed.The court recalled that it had, during the previous hearing, specifically directed FDA officials to apply their minds and take a pragmatic approach to the licence issue.“However, despite clearly saying this, the FDA has disobeyed our order and taken a pedantic view instead of a pragmatic view. We are tired of scolding the department and officers all the time. It is now time to pass stinging orders. We will issue contempt action against the concerned officers. Let them convince us or go to jail," the court said.The bench also questioned why the FDA acted with “undue haste” without fully analysing the legal position.“How many times should we try to convince and balance equities so that the department does not feel discouraged? Why do we say don't kill a mosquito with a sword? Do you feel you are a lord and you can do anything?” HC questioned.The dispute began after the FDA suspended the five licences last week. At Tuesday’s hearing, the HC had praised FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe’s drive against hygiene lapses but asked the department to “be consistent” and “do it consistently and not in an ad hoc manner”.The court had ordered a fresh inspection while declining to stay the suspensions, though it allowed MCA to serve tea and coffee through vending machines as a temporary arrangement during ongoing tournaments.
Article Summary: The bombay high court on slammed the maharashtra food and drug administration (fda) the department refused to lift the suspension of food licences of five restaurants at the mumbai cricket association (mca) premises. The mca had challenged the fda’s decision to suspend the restaurants’ licences over alleged hygiene violations.

Article Title: Present tense, future perfect: Zurich Airport sees 'slower ramp-up' in Noida Airport traffic
Article Text:
Dilli door ast (Photo: Saurabh Sinha)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Zurich Airport has prepared itself for a longer takeoff roll at Noida Airport before the traffic here takes off. Multiple factors like the last-minute pullout by on of the three launch airlines; Delhi's IGI Airport operating way below its existing and still expandable capacity and Noida International Airport's (NIA) connectivity woes with Delhi have meant a much lower than originally expected air traffic at the new hub that stated operations on June 15. Zurich Airport International AG is NIA's primary developer and concessionaire.Zurich Airport has said in its outlook for NIA: "Slower ramp up expected due to challenging geo political environment with near time performance remaining subject to elevated uncertainty. Route network will continue to expand with international services expected to follow. Strong confidence in the long term growth potential and attractive fundamentals of the Indian aviation market."It said NIA saw 104 flights and 25,000 passengers in June. This rose to 1,044 flights and 77,000 passengers in July. The airport's HY 16 EBIDTA loss is estimated about $3 million.IndiGo is the biggest operator at NIA, with Akasa having a few flights. Air India Express, which was to be the third launch airlines, had pulled out due to mounting losses of AI group. Setting up a new base means incurring significant expense, something AI wanted to avoid at this time.The going was never going to be easy for NIA, the first second airport to open in an Indian urban conglomerate without either the pre-existing hub operating to capacity (like Mumbai CSMIA); being constrained (like Goa Dabolim) or the older one shutting down (like Bengaluru HAL, Hyderabad Begumpet and Visakhapatnam when Bhogapuram opens in a couple of months). The new airports in Hyderabad and Bengaluru are almost as far as Delhiites find NIA to be but travellers simply didn’t have any option but to trudge the distance. Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida and Ghaziabad, however, have an option that’s closer, better connected and more affordable multi modal transport.When it was coming up amid the boom post Covid boom in air travel, NIA was expected to have a tough time till 2030 when IGIA was to saturate by reaching its peak capacity of about 13-14 crore passengers annually (CPA). IGIA currently has a capacity of 11 CPA and handled less than 8 crore passengers last year.Delhi Airport handles about 1,300 flights daily, way short of the 1,550 seen during the heady days of G20.So NIA would have to compete to get traffic with peak traffic hour slot availability being its USP to attract airlines. But it opened at a time when Indian carriers are reeling under the triple impact of finding lucrative western routes become unviable for them due to closure of Pakistan airspace for them since last April, US-Iran war sending oil prices flaring and the rupee weakening. As a result, they are cutting flights.
Article Summary: Zurich airport has said in its outlook for nia: "slower ramp up expected due to challenging geo political environment" noida international airport's (nia) connectivity woes with delhi have meant a much lower than originally expected air traffic. Indigo is the biggest operator at nia, with akasa having a few flights.

Article Title: 'Suddhikaran another name for untouchability': Rahul Gandhi accuses BJP, RSS of discrimination against Kharge
Article Text:
Rahul alleges BJP of discriminatory politics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh over a recent 'suddhikaran' or 'purification' ritual held at a venue in Uttarakhand where Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge had addressed a rally.Calling the practice "another name for untouchability", Rahul alleged that such an act was a crime under the Constitution.Addressing a presser at Congress headquarters in Delhi, the Rae Bareli MP said the country was witnessing a political contest between the ideology of the Constitution and that of the BJP and RSS."Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a 'purification' ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there. Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS," Rahul said."Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under India's Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. 'Purification' is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practice it openly," he added.Former Congress president said the ritual suggested that Dalits were "unclean" and should not be touched."When they perform this purification, they are effectively saying that Dalits should not be touched, that Dalits are unclean, and this constitutes a crime under the Indian Constitution," he said.Rahul also said the larger political contest in the country was between two opposing ideologies."A fight is under way in the country between two ideologies. On one side is the Constitution of India, the Constitution of Ambedkar, Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel. On the other is the ideology of the BJP and RSS. The politics currently playing out in India is between these two ideologies," Rahul said.He also spoke about alleged caste-based discrimination and said Dalits continue to face discrimination despite constitutional safeguards."For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors," he said."Just think about the impact this has on the minds of the future generation: children see some of their peers sweeping, while those doing the sweeping see others who do not have to do so. This is the reality of India," he added.Congress leader further alleged that caste discrimination was also visible in access to common resources such as water."Dalits are not allowed to drink water from the village well; they have had to dig their own private wells because they were barred from using the common village well," Rahul claimed.He also alleged that caste discrimination could be seen at tea stalls."At tea stalls, you see two types of cups in use: a reusable glass cup that can be washed, and a paper or plastic cup that is discarded after use. The plastic or paper cups are for Dalits, while the glass ones are for others," he alleged."This is the reality of India. This is the reality of Uttar Pradesh, the reality of North India, and you can see this in cities and villages," Rahul added.The Haldwani controversy relates to a Congress rally held at Ramlila Maidan on August 8, ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand assembly elections. Members of a right-wing group later performed a purification ritual at the venue, drawing criticism from Congress leaders.Kharge also raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, linking the incident to his identity as a Dalit leader and alleging that it was an attempt to portray him as "untouchable".Kharge said he did not mention any community or religion during his speech at the venue."But after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage. You may have read about this in the newspapers. Is this the way things should happen in a democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution?" Kharge had said.He later took to X and said he did not want the incident to be politicised, while calling for strict legal action and demanding that a case be filed under the Untouchability Act against those who conducted the ritual.
Article Summary: Rahul alleges bjp of discriminatory politics. Calls the practice "another name for untouchability", rahul alleged that such an act was a crime under the constitution. He also spoke about alleged caste-based discrimination and said dalits continue to face discrimination despite constitutional safeguards.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, reiterating the Congress' demand to maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 for another 25 years.Kharge's letter came after Union parliamentary affairs minister hinted at a possible special session of Parliament for the passage of the Delimitation Bill.In his letter, Kharge urged the government to convene an all-party meeting to discuss its proposed delimitation exercise before any such session."I have written to PM Modi on delimitation, the delay in prorogation of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, and the likely special session mentioned by the Union minister of parliamentary affairs in a television interview last evening," Kharge said."I had last written to you on July 16, 2026 requesting you to convene an All-Party meeting for discussing the Government's proposals for delimitation. I had also requested you to give all political parties adequate time to study such proposals in detail before they are introduced in any special session of Parliament that you may be contemplating," he added.Kharge also urged PM Modi to maintain the state-wise strength in Lok Sabha for another 25 years and introduce one-third reservation for women from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections."Maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 for another 25 years; Maintain the existing state-wise strength in the Lok Sabha for another 25 years; "Introduce one-third reservation for women from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Kharge reiterated his demand that the government convene an all-party meeting and give political parties and state governments adequate time to examine the proposals."This is an issue that has enormous significance for the country. Please do not again try and bulldoze as you attempted on April 16 and 17, 2026," Kharge said.

Article Title: 'Cordial discussions': JP Nadda meets anti-reservation group after Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan, which is protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at the national capital's Jantar Mantar.In a social media post on X, Nadda said that he met Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan as per the pre-determined schedule, adding that another meeting will be held soon."Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on August 21, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Shri Harsh Dubey, Shri Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Shri Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," he said.However, Nadda did not give details of the meeting.Meanwhile, Harsh Dubey said that the meeting was an important step towards dialogue."Positive initiative for the welfare of all society today. Our team met with the honourable Shri JP Nadda Ji. During this time, there was a brief discussion with him regarding the demonstration that took place on August 21. This meeting is an important step towards dialogue.We will soon meet again with the honourable Nadda Ji and strive to move forward with a positive and just decision in the interest of all society," Dubey said."Our objective is not against any section, but rather to democratically and peacefully present our views for equal opportunities, a just system, and necessary reforms in the national interest. Further information and decisions regarding this will be officially communicated shortly," he added.Reservation Hatao Andolan is demanding that quotas in academics and employment should strictly be determined by income levels rather than social or caste identities. Additionally, the protesters advocated for a "one family, one reservation" policy and demanded the immediate withdrawal of the UGC's 2026 caste-equity directives.A large number of people gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Friday to protest against caste-based reservation, following which the Delhi Police and Central Forces were deployed at the protest site to maintain law and order.Security personnel were seen present at Jantar Mantar as protesters assembled at the designated protest area. The police deployment was carried out as a precautionary measure amid the large gathering.Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) is an official Instagram page with 5.6 million followers. The platform rapidly gained traction by adopting the protest-mobilisation tactics of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and has now called for a physical protest against the reservation system.
Article Summary: Union minister jp nadda met representatives of reservation hatao andolan. Protesters are protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding overhaul at jantar mantar. Harsh dubey, mrityunjay pathak and ran bahadur singh chauhan attended the meeting.

Article Title: Caste count method in Census ‘misleading’: Congress letter to PM
Article Text:
The letter from Kharge and Rahul said govt should prepare a fresh questionnaire through consultations with parties.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Terming the methodology for caste count adopted in Census 2027 “misleading” as it will not give a headcount of OBCs, leaders of opposition in Parliament, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, have written to PM Narendra Modi demanding the Census questionnaire on caste notified recently be abandoned and a new one be drafted. They underlined that the word “OBC” has not even been used in the Census.In the backdrop of the controversy triggered by the questionnaire, Kharge and Rahul told the PM “your govt” has adopted an “open-ended question” to collect information about caste, and enumerators will have to take for an answer whatever a person replies to the caste question. They argued that a caste is known by different names and sub-castes depending on the region, which would result in one caste being recorded by thousands of names. “This would result in lakhs of castes being registered in the country, and the entire data recorded in the caste census would become useless,” the letter said.“We don’t approve of the caste census being done through this methodology. Govt should cancel the present questionnaire and prepare a fresh one through consultations with political parties, experts, and the public so that a correct headcount of every caste and community is collected and the caste census is precise, relevant, and beneficial,” it said.It said a readymade solution to the problem is that a “drop-down menu” comprising a list of castes be added to the questionnaire. “This very methodology is used for counting SCs and STs (in Census)... This methodology was adopted in the surveys of Bihar and Telangana. We are enclosing the caste lists of the two surveys for understanding.” Further, the letter said such a list of castes for Census can easily be compiled on the basis of the existing Socially and Educationally Backward Classes list and data from the Anthropological Survey of India.Releasing the letter, AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and OBC department chairperson Anil Jaihind said govt had, in an affidavit to SC in Sept 2021, submitted that a “drop-down menu” with a list of castes will have to be used if a caste census were to be done. Ramesh said census enumerators can carry the said list of OBCs and record precise answers. He accused govt of “sabotaging” the caste census.
Article Summary: The letter from kharge and rahul said govt should prepare a fresh questionnaire through consultations with parties. They underlined that the word “obc’ has not even been used in the census. Aicc spokesperson jairam ramesh and obc department chairperson anil jaihind accused govt of ‘sabotaging’ the caste census.

Article Title: Garg Aviation’s trainer aircraft crashes in Kanpur, 2 killed
Article Text:
An official examines the wreckage of a Tecnam aircraft following a fatal crash in Kanpur.

NEW DELHI: A training aircraft belonging to Kanpur’s Garg Aviation crashed on Thursday, killing two — an instructor and a trainee pilot — on board. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation said in a statement the Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft (VT-NBV) crashed about five nautical miles from Kanpur Civil Airport, near Ganga Barrage.“The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident. A team of three officials from the DGCA is proceeding to the site for necessary regulatory oversight and coordination,” said the DGCA statement.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation,” it added.Senior pilots call for a thorough investigation into the flying school operations.On June 26, 2026, a trainee pilot had got grievously injured while deboarding VT-NBV with the propeller running at Kanpur’s Chakeri Airport. Following this lapse, the DGCA had on June 28 said in a statement that it had “directed VT-NBV aircraft should not be utilised pending the probe.” Subsequently the aircraft started flying again till it crashed on Thursday.
Article Summary: The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of kanpur civil airport. The aircraft accident investigation bureau (aaib) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules”

Article Title: Nepal flood: Centre puts Bihar & UP on high alert as NDRF deploys teams
Article Text:
Flash floods in Nepal have triggered alerts in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In view of the flash flood situation in Nepal, Union home minister Amit Shah Wednesday spoke with CMs of Bihar and UP and assured all help to border districts, including deployment of additional National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams. The administrations of these districts have been put on high alert.“Govt of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis. I spoke with CMs of Bihar and UP regarding the disaster in Nepal. In border areas likely to be affected, local administration and rescue teams, along with NDRF, have been placed on high alert,” Shah said on X, expressing condolences to families of those who lost their loved ones in the disaster.Officers of home affairs, external affairs, jal shakti and defence ministries are monitoring the situation.Water level on Nepal-side reservoirs is reducing and the situation is under control. No panic-like situation has arisen, according to Central Water Commission (CWC).NDRF had earlier said the flash floods in the Nepal-China border region has led to a sudden rise in water level in Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal, around 160 km from the Indian border, and the flood wave is likely to travel downstream in Gandak river.“Local authorities in Bihar and UP near the India-Nepal border along Gandak river have been advised to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the situation,” NDRF said. In close coordination with the states and CWC, NDRF is keeping a close watch on the situation and has kept additional teams on standby for emergent requirements in case of any “unforeseen” situation.Out of nine NDRF teams deployed in Bihar, two have been dispatched for deployment in West Champaran and Muzaffarpur. The state govt is monitoring the situation and, in case of requirement, additional teams will be deployed.
Article Summary: Flash floods in nepal have triggered alerts in uttar pradesh and bihar. Water level on nepal-side reservoirs is reducing and the situation is under control. No panic-like situation has arisen, according to central water commission (cwc) ndrf is keeping a close watch on the situation and has kept additional teams on standby.

Article Title: Day after Farooq dare, Srinagar MP Mehdi decides to quit Lok Sabha, NC over Article 370
Article Text:
NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announces resignation from Lok Sabha and party after Farooq Abdullah's public dare to contest on his own.

SRINAGAR: National Conference’s Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announced Friday that he would resign from both Lok Sabha and the party, taking up patriarch Farooq Abdullah’s public dare to quit and contest an election on his own instead of criticising the brass repeatedly over its alleged dilution of the campaign for restoration of Article 370.Mehdi said he would formally send his resignation to LS Speaker Om Birla on Nov 3, coinciding with the 26th death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was killed by terrorists.In a letter to Farooq, who remains NC president, Mehdi flagged what he sees as a dichotomy in the party’s stand on constitutional guarantees for the region. “I remember that you were the chief minister of the very assembly that passed the autonomy resolution. That, too, must have required courage. Why, then, has the mere mention of constitutional guarantees for Jammu & Kashmir now become so offensive that you felt compelled to publicly demand my resignation?”The MP described Article 370, struck off on Aug 5, 2019, as part of the decision to revoke J&K’s special status, as “shorthand for the struggle to restore the dignity, honour, constitutional guarantees and liberties” of Kashmiris.“Nearly 65% of J&K’s population is young, and their future is increasingly uncertain, with no jobs and opportunities. Our land is up for grabs. Our resources benefit everybody but us. Our religious rights, traditions and language face constant pressure,” Mehdi wrote.The MP has been increasingly critical of CM Omar Abdullah and NC for allegedly narrowing their fight to statehood and business rules for governance.Although a member of the party’s working committee, he hasn’t been part of crucial meetings.His rift with the party deepened after Dec 23, 2024, when he led a large student protest outside Omar’s Gupkar residence against the UT’s reservation policy. Omar engaged five student representatives in a long discussion but ignored Mehdi.Earlier this week, Farooq said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary election without NC and accused him of trying to project himself as a powerful votary of Article 370 while being “on the wrong path”.
Article Summary: Nc mp aga ruhullah mehdi announces resignation from lok sabha and party after farooq abdullah's public dare to contest on his own. Mehdi flagged what he sees as a dichotomy in the party’s stand on constitutional guarantees for the region.

Article Title: The Dalit enigma: Why Mayawati is going solo in Punjab
Article Text:
Mayawati’s solo Punjab gamble tests whether the state’s 32% Dalit population can translate into a consolidated BSP vote.

Punjab's number paradox

In Punjab, Dalits are divided into several sub-castes and religion.

From Kanshi Ram's Punjab to BSP's high-water mark

Mayawati pays tribute on death anniversary of Kanshi Ram.

How 2022 exposed the paradox

SAD and its alliance route

AAP's pitch: Welfare, not identity

Congress has history, but not the Dalit lock

Mayawati's real gamble

Ready to play a spoilsport?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bahujan Samaj Party ( BSP ) chief Mayawati has decided to go solo in the upcoming 2027 Punjab assembly election. This move has put the spotlight on a striking contradiction in the state's politics: Punjab has India's highest proportion of Scheduled Castes, but no political party has been able to turn that numerical strength into a durable Dalit vote bloc.On August 25, Mayawati announced that the BSP would contest the polls "alone without any alliance or compromise with anyone", arguing that electoral tie-ups risked weakening the party’s vote share and demoralising its cadre.The decision carries particular significance in Punjab, where BSP founder Kanshi Ram began his political journey and where Scheduled Castes account for 31.94% of the population, according to the 2011 Census.Yet nearly one-third of Punjab's population has never translated into nearly one-third of the vote for the BSP - or any other Dalit-centric political formation.Instead, the Dalit electorate has remained divided across caste, religious, regional and economic lines, allowing the Congress, AAP, SAD and BJP to each build pockets of support within it.That makes Mayawati's 2027 gamble less about the size of Punjab's Dalit population and more about a difficult political question: Can she turn the state's 32% Dalit population into a coherent electoral bloc?The numbers explain why every major political party wants a share of the Dalit vote. Punjab had about 88.6 lakh Scheduled Castes in the 2011 Census, accounting for 31.94% of its population - the highest SC proportion among Indian states. The community is particularly concentrated in the Doaba region, which includes Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur and Nawanshahr.Eight of Doaba's 23 assembly constituencies are reserved for SC candidates, while both Lok Sabha constituencies in the region, Jalandhar and Hoshiarpur, are reserved.Across Punjab, 34 of the 117 assembly seats are reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. But the political influence of Dalit voters extends far beyond these constituencies.A 2021 analysis by Lokniti-CSDS professor Sanjay Kumar found that Dalits accounted for more than 30% of voters in 54 assembly constituencies and between 20% and 30% in another 45.In other words, Dalit voters can influence far more than the 34 seats formally reserved for them.But there is a crucial caveat: 'Dalit' is not a single political identity in Punjab.The community comprises several sub-caste and religious groups, including Ravidassias/Ad-Dharmis, Mazhabi Sikhs, Ramdasias and others. Their geographical distribution, religious affiliations, economic circumstances and political histories differ.That fragmentation has repeatedly prevented the kind of consolidated Dalit politics that emerged around the BSP in Uttar Pradesh.Punjab's agrarian structure adds another layer. Land and economic power remain disproportionately concentrated among dominant agrarian communities, particularly Jat Sikhs. As a result, Dalit politics in the state often revolves around land rights, employment, reservation, social dignity and access to common resources, rather than caste identity alone.The irony is that Punjab was once among the BSP's strongest political laboratories.Kanshi Ram, born in Punjab, built his early political movement around the mobilisation of Scheduled Castes and other marginalised communities before founding the BSP in 1984.The party's breakthrough in Punjab came in the 1992 election. It won nine of the state's 117 seats with 16.32% of the vote, emerging as the principal opposition party in the House. Six of those nine seats came from Doaba, underlining the region’s importance to the party’s political project.But the breakthrough proved difficult to sustain.In 1997, the BSP's tally fell to one seat, although it still secured 7.48% of the vote. Its vote share then declined steadily — to 5.69% in 2002, 4.13% in 2007 and 4.29% in 2012. By 2017, it had fallen to 1.52%.In 2022, the BSP won just one seat with 1.77% of the vote, contesting as part of its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal.The steep decline in three decades captures the central problem Mayawati now faces.If the BSP's decline showed the difficulty of sustaining Dalit-centric politics, the 2022 assembly election demonstrated how effectively mainstream parties can cut across caste identities.The AAP won 92 of Punjab's 117 seats with 42.01% of the statewide vote, while Congress was reduced to 18 seats.The AAP’s performance was particularly striking in SC-reserved constituencies. It won 29 of the 34 reserved seats, while Congress won four and the SAD-BSP alliance one.The result also undercut the assumption that Congress's elevation of Charanjit Singh Channi as Punjab's first Dalit CM would automatically consolidate the Dalit vote behind the party. Channi became CM in September 2021, just months before the election. His elevation was widely viewed as an attempt to appeal to the state’s huge Dalit electorate.But in March 2022, Congress suffered a dramatic defeat.The SAD has historically had its own Dalit support base, particularly among Sikh Dalits.Its alliance with Mayawati ahead of the 2022 election was an attempt to combine the Akali network among sections of the Sikh electorate with the BSP's Dalit support base.The combination, however, failed to produce the revival the two parties had hoped for. The alliance won four seats - three for the SAD and one for the BSP - with a combined vote share of around 20%.BJP's gamble: From alliance politics to going soloThe BJP faces perhaps the most difficult social-coalition challenge of all.Its long-standing electoral arrangement with the SAD ended after the Akali Dal walked out of the NDA at the Centre over the farm laws.The BJP is now trying to establish itself as an independent force in a state where it historically relied heavily on the Akali alliance to provide it with a rural and Sikh social base. That means the party needs to build coalitions beyond the constituencies it traditionally relied on, while also trying to repair its relationship with farmers.Dalit voters are an obvious part of that expansion strategy.But Punjab is not Uttar Pradesh or Bihar. There, the BJP has invested heavily in a social coalition involving non-Yadav OBCs and Dalits. A different caste and religious configuration shapes Punjab’s political landscape, while its agrarian structure and Sikh identity make the BJP’s social engineering considerably more complicated.For the BJP, winning Dalit voters is therefore not simply about adding another community to its support base. It is about constructing an entirely new political coalition in a state where its old alliance no longer provides the same electoral cushion.The AAP has already demonstrated why the size of the Dalit population does not automatically translate into BSP votes.In 2022, the party's appeal cut across caste lines, combining welfare, anti-incumbency and the promise of an alternative to the traditional parties. It also had the 'Delhi model' to demonstrate its pitch.AAP sought to build a political vocabulary around BR Ambedkar, combining Ambedkarite symbolism with a broader welfare narrative.Rather than presenting Dalits as a separate electoral constituency, the party has sought to fold their concerns into a larger promise around government schools, healthcare, jobs, welfare delivery and social dignity.However, now the 2027 election will test whether AAP can retain that support after a full term in government.Congress has historically had a strong base among both Hindu and Sikh Dalits in Punjab, but its 2022 performance showed the limits of that advantage. In the 2017 election, the party won 21 of 34 SC-reserved seats; by 2022, after making Charanjit Singh Channi the state’s first Dalit CM and projecting him as its CM face, Congress was reduced to just four reserved seats, while AAP won 29.The setback has not ended Congress's Dalit outreach. In January 2026, Channi himself raised questions within the party over the representation of Dalit leaders, pointing out that several key Punjab Congress positions were held by Jat Sikhs.For Congress, the 2027 challenge is therefore not winning Dalit votes from scratch, but rebuilding a social coalition it once had, without reducing Dalit politics to the Channi factor alone.Mayawati’s decision to contest alone is therefore both ideological and organisational.The BSP has something only a few parties can claim: a political vocabulary explicitly built around Ambedkar, Kanshi Ram and Bahujan mobilisation. Punjab also provides the demographic foundation for such a project.But the party’s electoral history demonstrates the enormous gap between having a potential social constituency and converting it into votes and seats.The challenge is not simply to persuade Dalits to vote for the BSP. It is to persuade different Dalit communities that their interests are sufficiently common to vote for the same party. That is a much harder proposition in Punjab than the 32% figure suggests.There is, however, another reason Mayawati’s decision could matter even if the BSP does not return to anything close to its 1992 performance.Punjab’s 2027 contest is shaping up as a fragmented battle involving AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD, although the possibility of a BJP-SAD reunion remains open.In such a contest, even a relatively small but geographically concentrated BSP vote could become consequential.The party’s past performance offers a warning to the larger parties. In 2024, the BSP was reported to have remained a significant factor in parts of Doaba despite its shrinking statewide base, with observers pointing to its potential to influence contests in seats such as Anandpur Sahib, Jalandhar and Hoshiarpur.That is the paradox of Mayawati's Punjab gamble.The BSP may no longer have the numbers to dominate Punjab’s Dalit politics, but it could still have enough votes to disrupt everyone else’s arithmetic.The 2027 election will therefore test not just whether Mayawati can revive the BSP in Kanshi Ram’s home state, but whether Punjab’s nearly 32% Dalit population can finally translate its demographic weight into political leverage - if not as a single bloc, then as the constituency no major party can afford to ignore.
Article Summary: Mayawati’s solo punjab gamble tests whether the state's 32% dalit population can translate into a consolidated bsp vote. Punjab has india's highest proportion of scheduled castes, but no political party has been able to turn that numerical strength into a durable dalit vote bloc.

Article Title: Flash floods put focus on India's glacial lakes
Article Text:
An aerial view of damaged structures covered in thick mud and debris following the flash floods at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) disaster in Nepal Wednesday has renewed discussion on India's own strategy and preparedness to mitigate such risk with the presence of approximately 200 high-risk glacial lakes in the Himalayan regions.According to govt's survey of these glacial lakes, Himalayan ranges are host to as many as 7,500 of them - with 10% in Sikkim and of which 25 are considered very high-risk. The study found 4,700 of these glacial lakes situated in Ganga river basin with a catchment area estimated at over 2.5 lakh sqkm, projecting a colossal scale of devastation a single breach could cause.India suffered one of the worst GLOF disasters in recent times when on Oct 3, 2023, glacial rocks of 14.7 cubic meter collapsed in South Lhonak Lake in Sikkim, close to midnight, "generating a 20-m high displacement wave", wiping out several hydro power assets and settlements on its way downstream.Krishna Vatsa, member of National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), said the Nepal event illustrates a new dimension of Himalayan disaster risk, though the precise sequence of events is still being scientifically established. "These are cascading hazards: an ice or rock failure can become a debris flow, create a temporary lake and then generate a flash flood. Such events can develop extremely rapidly and may provide very little warning time downstream."India's National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme has marked 195 at-risk glacial lakes and follows five key priorities (assessment, monitoring, early warning, mitigation, community awareness). It needs to be speeded up and scaled up immediately as a priority for national security," said Syed Safi Ahsan Rizvi, an ex-NDMA member.As a response to the Sikkim disaster, Centre had set up a high-level coordination committee on GLOF disaster risk reduction. The initiative, spearheaded by PM's principal secretary PK Mishra, was tasked to host multi-agency deliberations and surveys of such lakes and identify the high-risk ones. Govt also allocated Rs 150 crore for the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme for four Himalayan states having high-risk glacial lakes.The first meeting of the coordination committee on DRR was held in Nov 2024, when PM's principal secretary expressing his satisfaction on the group's "tri-focal lens: assessment, monitoring, and mitigation". The committee hosted regular meetings and received feedback, which were then formed as part of joint strategy between states and Centre. However, not much is known on follow up actions.Earlier, govt had claimed that multi-agency expeditions were conducted to assess all "A-category" lakes. The teams comprised scientists and officials from NDMA, Central Water Commission, Geological Survey of India, Centre for Development of Advance Computing, ITBP and the Army.
Article Summary: Himalayan ranges are host to as many as 7,500 of them - with 10% in sikkim and of which 25 are considered very high-risk. Study found 4,700 of these glacial lakes situated in ganga river basin with catchment area estimated at over 2.5 lakh sqkm.

Article Title: From Reds to NGOs: RSS weekly expands ‘dimagi Naxal’ label

‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”

NEW DELHI: The RSS has joined the campaign against “dimagi Naxals” which PM Modi launched on Aug 15, with its affiliated weekly ‘Organiser’ arguing that the Sonia Gandhi-led National Advisory Council (NAC) under UPA allowed Maoist-influenced thinking to enter policymaking.In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.The weekly stopped short of accusing Sonia or Congress brass of links with Maoists, directing its criticism at NAC and the ideological influence the body brought into governance.It distinguishes “dimagi Naxals” from ordinary agitators or reform groups, acknowledging issues such as education and climate change can be genuine while alleging such concerns may be appropriated by an ideological core. In his I-Day speech, PM said armed Naxalism was nearing its end but people subscribing to the ideology who entered govt panels as advisers were still looking to create violence and anarchy.That reference also appeared to recall UPA-era controversies involving human rights activist Binayak Sen.Sen, arrested in 2007, was nominated to the Planning Commission steering committee on health in 2011.The govt has sought to draw a boundary around the expression. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said Modi was not accusing opposition netas or parties, but referring to those supporting Maoists, who reject Constitution and back separatism.Set up in 2004 and chaired by Sonia Gandhi with cabinet-rank status, NAC brought activists, academics and experts into policymaking and played an important role in measures such as RTI and MGNREGA.
Article Summary: ‘organiser’ termed nac as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi naxals’ of governance’ the editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and ngos formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”

Article Title: Valmiki scam: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns; breaks down on camera
Article Text:
B Nagendra broke down during a press conference while announcing his decision

Pressure after cabinet re-induction

What is the Valmiki Corporation case?

NEW DELHI: Karnataka planning and statistics minister B Nagendra resigned from the state cabinet on Friday amid mounting pressure over the alleged Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam.He also broke down during a press conference while announcing his decision.Nagendra stepped down within 25 days of assuming office after being re-inducted into the cabinet on August 3. He said he had tendered his resignation to chief minister D K Shivakumar."Today I am voluntarily tendering my resignation as the minister," an emotional Nagendra told reporters.He said he had taken the decision with a heavy heart to ensure that the party leadership was not embarrassed.Nagendra alleged that he was being targeted as part of a conspiracy and said the BJP could not intimidate him through central investigating agencies."They (BJP) can't scare me with ED, CBI," Nagendra said.He also alleged that "Manuwadis", in an apparent reference to the BJP, were targeting him because they did not want a tribal person in the country to grow."Manuwadis targeted me as they didn't want a tribal person in the country to grow," he alleged.Nagendra also challenged the BJP to defeat him in Ballari in the "court of public opinion". He said he was prepared to resign as an MLA and face elections if the BJP was ready to take him on.The resignation marks the second time Nagendra has stepped down from the cabinet over the controversy. He had earlier resigned as tribal welfare minister in June 2024 when the issue first surfaced.Nagendra was re-inducted into the Karnataka cabinet on August 3 and given the planning and statistics portfolio. His return triggered fresh demands from the BJP and JD(S) for his removal over the alleged diversion of funds from the state-run corporation.Earlier on Friday, Nagendra had said he would meet chief minister D K Shivakumar and discuss the matter in detail."If a situation arises where my actions cause embarrassment to the party, then I will..." he had said, alleging that the developments were part of a "conspiracy".The opposition BJP and JD(S) had been protesting his re-induction into the cabinet and alleging his involvement in the alleged Rs 89 crore scam.The two parties had also staged repeated protests inside and outside the Karnataka legislature during the recent monsoon session, which was curtailed by three days and adjourned sine die on August 24 amid continued disruptions.The BJP and JD(S) had planned a foot march from Raichur to Ballari from September 1 to 10, demanding Nagendra's resignation.The controversy dates back to May 2024, when P Chandrasekharan, then an accounts superintendent with the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation, died by suicide and left behind a six-page note alleging irregularities and unauthorised transfers of corporation funds.Subsequent investigations found that Rs 89.63 crore had been transferred from a corporation account to a Union Bank of India account and later moved to multiple other accounts, triggering a major political controversy.Nagendra, who was tribal welfare minister when the issue surfaced, resigned from the cabinet in June 2024.He had previously rejected reports that he would resign and maintained that the allegations against him were "politically motivated". Just two days ago, he had dismissed media reports claiming that he had offered to step down.His resignation on Friday came amid renewed political pressure on the Congress government over the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam.
Article Summary: B nagendra broke down during a press conference while announcing his decision. He said he had taken the decision with a heavy heart to ensure that the party leadership was not embarrassed. Nagendra alleged that he was being targeted as part of a conspiracy and said the bjp could not intimidate him through central investigating agencies.

Article Title: Junk foods will soon have labels warning of high salt, sugar and fat
Article Text:
FSSAI agrees to red hexagonal warning labels on junk food packages for high salt, sugar and fat content.

Do warning labels work?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Junk foods will soon carry warning labels highlighting high levels of salt, sugar and fat, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) telling Supreme Court on Friday that it has agreed to red-coloured hexagonal warnings on the front of food packages to help consumers identify products high in specified nutrients of concern.FSSAI conveyed its position through a compliance affidavit filed before Supreme Court in response to the court's Aug 13 order on front-of-pack labelling (FoPL).The move comes after the court pushed Centre to act on the issue, saying, "If the Union does it on its own, well and good, otherwise we shall proceed to pass further directions."Under the framework, products high in specified nutrients would carry prominent red hexagonal warnings reading "HIGH FAT", "HIGH SALT" and/or "HIGH SUGAR", as applicable.FSSAI has agreed to exempt single-ingredient foods such as ghee, edible oil, salt, sugar, jaggery and honey from the proposed warnings, subject to applicable food safety and labelling regulations.The regulator has agreed to implement FoPL in phases, giving the industry time to reformulate products. Phase I would cover products high in two or more specified nutrients, while Phase II would extend warnings to products high in any one specified nutrient.The framework is based on nutrient thresholds specified under the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, issued by ICMR-NIN. The affidavit follows the Supreme Court’s observations on public health, particularly amid concerns over the rising prevalence of childhood obesity. The court said front-of-pack labelling could help consumers make informed purchasing decisions.The case stems from a PIL filed by NGO 3S and Our Health Society, which approached Supreme Court through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dwivedi, seeking front-of-pack labelling to help consumers make informed choices.FSSAI said the system is intended to provide a “simple, prominent and easily comprehensible warning” to consumers about food products high in specified nutrients of concern. It also cited international examples, including Chile and Canada, where front-of-pack labelling has been adopted.Supreme Court had considered options including coloured indicators, interpretative words, numbers, letters, symbols and percentages for front-of-pack labelling and directed Centre to take a decision and place it on record.
Article Summary: Fssai agrees to red hexagonal warning labels on junk food packages for high salt, sugar and fat content. Move comes after the court pushed centre to act on the issue. The case stems from a pil filed by ngo 3s and our health society.

Article Title: Clean energy push unfair on developing nations: CJI Surya Kant
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant said clean energy push unfair on developing nations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant on Friday told Commonwealth Countries that it is unfair that the industrialised countries, who took two centuries to adopt clean energy, are asking the nations in the process of industrialisation to move towards renewable energy within decades.Speaking at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, CJI Kant said, “Countries that are finally industrialising are being asked to move rapidly towards renewable power, and often made to bear the brunt of criticism when they cannot move fast enough. In comparison, the nations urging that transition spent two centuries building their own strength on coal and oil,” he said.Addressing the common platform for 56 countries on “Policy dialogue on climate justice”, the CJI said the cumulative shift of commonwealth countries to clean energy depends on copper, cobalt and lithium, extraction of which carries environmental and social consequences.Developing countries facing myriad challenges depending on their geographical locations and pushing them towards clean energy at an unrealistic pace could create more challenges than solutions, he warned.Justice Kant said, “The challenge, therefore, is to reconcile the urgency of the clean energy transition with the principles of fairness and shared responsibility that must underpin it.”He said the Supreme Court of India and the HCs have played a significant role in protecting the environment, ecology and its endangered species.He recounted the Zambian HC making a copper mining company liable for polluting water. Commonwealth countries can learn from each other’s experience to bolster efforts towards smoother transition towards clean energy without making their populations pay a heavy price, he said.“We need not develop a separate jurisprudential vocabulary in every country where a climate question reaches the Courts. Rather, the Courts should be open to borrowing ideas, approaches, and solutions that have proved useful elsewhere in the Commonwealth, while adapting them carefully to their own constitutional, social, and environmental circumstances,” he said.“Courts must be willing to search for solutions that protect the environment without losing sight of the legitimate needs of development, and to recognise that the two need not always be cast as choices in which one must defeat the other,” CJI Kant said.He cited the case before SC where the officials were accused of felling many trees to widen a road for access to a super specialty hospital for wounded para-military forces. “We had no wish to reward officials who had cut trees; equally, we had no wish to deny wounded soldiers an ambulance route,” he said.Instead of halting the widening of roads, the SC had ordered extensive compensatory afforestation. “We still monitoring that afforestation today… development and preservation do not always have to stand on opposite sides of the scales. Sometimes, the task of a Court is to find the third way to promote both routes through judicial creativity,” he said.
Article Summary: Cji surya kant said clean energy push unfair on developing nations. Cji said the cumulative shift of commonwealth countries to clean energy depends on copper, cobalt and lithium, extraction of which carries environmental and social consequences.

Article Title: Two resignations, same scam: Why B Nagendra quit Karnataka cabinet again
Article Text:
This is B Nagendra's second resignation in over two years.​

Second resignation in over two years

What is

Valmiki scam

?

NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister B Nagendra announced his decision to resign from the state cabinet on Friday, just 25 days after assuming office, amid mounting pressure over his alleged involvement in the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribe Development Corporation financial irregularities.Addressing a press conference, teary-eyed Nagendra said that he was innocent and had been unfairly targeted by the opposition."I am resigning of my own will to avoid the embarrassment that may cost my party because of unnecessary allegations made by the opposition party against me," Nagendra said."Manuwadis (apparently referring to the BJP) targeted me as they didn't want a tribal person in the country to grow," he added.This comes after Bharatiya Janata Party and JD(S) had been demanding Nagendra's resignation over the alleged scam and had planned a foot march from Raichur to Ballari from September 1 to 10.The opposition had also staged repeated protests inside and outside the Karnataka Vidhan Saudha during the monsoon session, which was curtailed by three days and adjourned sine die on August 24 amid the continued uproar.This is Nagendra's second resignation from the cabinet over the same allegations.Earlier, in June 2024, Nagendra had resigned from the tribal welfare department in Siddaramaiah's cabinet after the controversy had surfaced.He was, however, re-inducted into DK Shivakumar's cabinet on August 3, 2026, with the planning and statistics portfolio, prompting the opposition to revive its demand for his removal.The Valmiki scam refers to the alleged illegal transfer of funds from the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation Ltd, a state-run body under the administrative control of the minister’s department.The alleged irregularities came to light following the suicide of accounts superintendent Chandrashekhar P on May 26, 2025. In his death note, Chandrashekhar alleged that Rs 187 crore belonging to the corporation had been unauthorisedly transferred from its bank account.Of this amount, Rs 88.62 crore was allegedly moved to various accounts, including those linked to prominent IT companies and a Hyderabad-based cooperative bank.The matter gained further momentum after Union Bank of India filed a complaint with the CBI, which subsequently registered an FIR and began investigating the alleged financial irregularities.Following the development, then chief minister Siddaramaiah and then state Congress president DKS reportedly met and sought the resignation of Nagendra, promising reinstatement if he was found not guilty.The state government also constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by Manish Kharbikar, additional director general of police, economic offences, at the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), to conduct a parallel probe.
Article Summary: This is b nagendra's second resignation from the cabinet over the same allegations. The valmiki scam refers to the alleged illegal transfer of funds from a state-run body. In june 2024, nagendra had resigned from the tribal welfare department in siddaramaiah's cabinet.
